definition: lasting for a very short time
example: Fame in the app store is ephemeral; most hits vanish within a month.

definition: present or found everywhere
example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous on campus.

definition: dealing with things sensibly and realistically
example: She took a pragmatic approach and shipped the simple fix first.

definition: open to more than one interpretation
example: The requirements were ambiguous, so the team asked for examples.

definition: showing great attention to detail
example: His meticulous notes made the exam review painless.

definition: able to recover quickly from difficulties
example: A resilient system keeps serving requests when a node dies.

definition: new or unusual in an interesting way
example: The paper proposes a novel caching strategy.

definition: too long, slow, or dull; tiresome
example: Manually renaming a thousand files is tedious; write a script.

definition: seeming reasonable or probable
example: The bug report offered a plausible explanation for the crash.

definition: not needed; superfluous, often as a backup
example: The redundant replica took over when the primary failed.

definition: based on random choice rather than reason
example: The 80-character limit feels arbitrary but keeps diffs readable.

definition: giving much information clearly in few words
example: A concise commit message saves every future reader a minute.

definition: logical and consistent
example: Her essay is coherent from thesis to conclusion.

definition: showing steady, earnest effort
example: Diligent review of flashcards beats cramming the night before.

definition: possible to do easily or conveniently
example: Shipping by Friday is feasible if we cut the extra screen.

definition: certain to happen; unavoidable
example: Merge conflicts are inevitable on a busy branch.

definition: very complicated or detailed
example: The scheduler's intricate logic deserved a diagram.

definition: expressed clearly; easy to understand
example: The textbook's lucid explanation finally made recursion click.

definition: no longer produced or used; out of date
example: The docs describe an obsolete flag that was removed last year.

definition: strong and healthy; able to withstand failure
example: Robust error handling turned the demo into a product.

definition: so delicate or precise as to be hard to notice
example: A subtle race condition only appeared under load.

definition: of little value or importance
example: The fix looked trivial but touched every call site.

definition: using more words than needed
example: Enable verbose logging only while debugging.

definition: capable of working successfully
example: A free tier makes the side project viable for students.

definition: truthful and straightforward; frank
example: Her candid feedback improved the draft immensely.

definition: to make suffering or a problem less severe
example: Caching alleviated the pressure on the database.

definition: to combine into a whole or total
example: The worker aggregates daily study stats every night.

definition: to entrust a task to another person
example: A good lead delegates the interesting problems too.

definition: to collect and assemble; to translate code
example: She compiled a reading list for the algorithms exam.

definition: to obtain something from a source
example: The level is derived from total experience points.

definition: to make or become less
example: Interruptions diminish the value of a focus session.

definition: to make an action or process easier
example: Shared rooms facilitate accountability among friends.

definition: to create difficulties resulting in delay
example: Notifications hinder deep work more than we admit.

definition: to suggest without saying directly
example: A green check implies the tests ran, not that they are good.

definition: to make something bad less severe
example: Rate limiting mitigates abuse from chatty clients.

definition: to make as effective as possible
example: Optimize the slow query before buying a bigger server.

definition: to continue firmly despite difficulty; to store durably
example: Presence is not persisted; it lives in Redis with a TTL.

definition: to suggest or assume as a basis for reasoning
example: The model postulates that focus decays after 90 minutes.

definition: to examine closely and critically
example: Reviewers scrutinized the migration before it touched prod.

definition: to combine parts into a coherent whole
example: The report synthesizes findings from five experiments.

definition: to check or prove the accuracy of
example: Always validate input at the boundary of the system.

definition: next to or adjoining something else
example: BFS visits all adjacent nodes before going deeper.

definition: something that deviates from what is normal
example: The metrics dashboard flagged an anomaly at 3am.

definition: general agreement among a group
example: The team reached consensus on the API shape.

definition: a standard by which something is judged
example: Latency is the main criterion for picking a region.

definition: a difficult choice between two options
example: The classic dilemma: ship fast or ship polished.

definition: a proposed explanation to be tested
example: The A/B test rejected our hypothesis about onboarding.

definition: a typical example or model of something
example: Functional programming is a different paradigm, not a library.

definition: the level at which something starts to happen
example: Alerts fire when error rate crosses the threshold.

definition: the path something follows over time
example: Two focused hours a day changes the trajectory of a semester.
